title: A bank balance sheet: required and excess reserves, lending and the money supply
scenario: Harbor Bank is a commercial bank in a banking system with limited reserves, where the reserve requirement limits lending: banks lend all of their excess reserves, and borrowers keep none of their loans as cash. Its balance sheet is shown below.

stimulus.title: Balance sheet of Harbor Bank
stimulus.html:
Balance sheet of the invented Harbor Bank, in dollars. The required reserve ratio is 0.2, and Harbor Bank has no other liabilities (invented data).
AssetsDollarsLiabilitiesDollars
Reserves150,000Checkable deposits500,000
Loans350,000

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Calculate Harbor Bank's required reserves. Show your work.
parts.sample: Required reserves = checkable deposits x required reserve ratio = $500,000 x 0.2 = $100,000.

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Calculate Harbor Bank's excess reserves. Show your work.

rubric.point: $150,000 - $100,000 = $50,000, with the work shown (or consistent with part A)

parts.sample: Excess reserves = total reserves - required reserves = $150,000 - $100,000 = $50,000.

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: Identify the maximum amount Harbor Bank can lend right now.

rubric.point: $50,000, its excess reserves (or consistent with part B)

parts.sample: Harbor Bank can lend at most its excess reserves, $50,000.

parts.label: D
parts.prompt: If Harbor Bank lends the amount in part C, calculate the maximum change in the money supply for the whole banking system. Show your work.

rubric.point: An increase of $50,000 x (1 / 0.2) = $250,000, with the money multiplier shown (or consistent with part C)

parts.sample: Money multiplier = 1 / 0.2 = 5. Maximum change in the money supply = $50,000 x 5 = $250,000 increase.

parts.label: E
parts.prompt: Separately, a customer deposits $10,000 of cash into a checking account at Harbor Bank. Explain what happens to the money supply (M1) at the moment of the deposit.

rubric.point: States that M1 does not change, because currency held by the public falls by the same $10,000 that checkable deposits rise
accept: no change because cash turns into a deposit

parts.sample: M1 does not change at the moment of the deposit. Currency held by the public falls by $10,000 and checkable deposits rise by $10,000, and both are part of M1. New money is created only later, if the bank lends its new excess reserves.
